chief_complaint: rapidly growing, friable red skin papule on finger that bleeds profusely with minor trauma
hpi_details: 28F pregnant woman presenting with a 1 cm pedunculated, bright vascular nodule on right thumb that bleeds spontaneously requiring shave excision and electrocautery base ablation.
ideas: She thinks a minor paper cut or splinter got infected and swelled into a large blood blister under the influence of her pregnancy hormones.
concerns: She is worried that the rapidly growing red nodule could be an aggressive skin cancer and fears that numbing injections or surgery might harm her developing baby.
expectations: She hopes the doctor can safely remove or burn off the bump today using pregnancy-safe numbing medicine so it stops bleeding all over her clothes.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Pyogenic Granuloma Excision evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Pyogenic Granuloma Excision is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Pyogenic Granuloma Excision, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Pyogenic Granuloma Excision.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Failing to send an excised or atypical lesion for histopathology, or to urgently reassess uncontrolled bleeding, infection, or recurrence.

reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Pyogenic Granuloma Excision.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Pyogenic Granuloma Excision.
reference_soap.plan: Confirm the clinical diagnosis and send excised tissue for histopathology when the diagnosis is uncertain or the lesion is atypical. For persistent bleeding, use direct pressure and seek urgent assessment if it does not stop. Local treatment or excision should be performed by a qualified clinician; discuss recurrence, wound care, and pregnancy-specific considerations with dermatology or the procedural team.

teaching.one_liner: Plastic and reconstructive surgical case presenting with rapidly growing, friable red skin papule on finger that bleeds profusely with minor trauma.

must_ask.objective: Onset relative to pregnancy or trauma
must_ask.say: When did this bump appear, and did it start after a cut or injury to the finger?
Does it bleed easily or spontaneously, even without touching it?
How quickly has it grown since you first noticed it?
Is the bump painful or tender when you touch it?

must_ask.objective: Pregnancy details and prior similar lesions
must_ask.say: How many weeks pregnant are you, and have you had a lesion like this before?

history.answer: I have a red bump on my right thumb that grew quickly and bleeds heavily whenever I bump or touch it.
I first noticed a tiny red dot about three weeks ago, and it has gotten much bigger since then.
It is right on the pad of my right thumb.
It grew very fast, going from a tiny speck to pea-sized in just two or three weeks.
It is about one centimeter across, and there is only this single bump on my hand.
It feels soft and fleshy on a tiny stalk, but it is firmly attached at the base.
It is slightly tender if pressed directly, but it does not cause severe throbbing pain.
It is bright red and shiny, and the surface looks moist and crusty after it bleeds.
It bleeds heavily with the slightest friction like catching on clothing, and it takes several minutes of firm pressure to stop.
I remember pricking that exact spot with a sewing needle about a month ago.
No, there is no pus, bad smell, or spreading warmth around my thumb.
No, there is no central dark pore or cheesy material coming out.
No, it has stayed swollen and has not shrunk at all.
I kept a bandage on it, but I have not tried popping or cutting it because of the bleeding.
No, I have never had any bumps like this before in my life.
No fevers, chills, unexplained weight loss, or swollen glands at all.
No, I work inside an office and have not had bad sunburns or heavy sun exposure.
No one in my family has had skin cancer or melanoma, and I do not have many moles.
No, I do not take immunosuppressive drugs, and I have not had any cat scratches or contact with sick animals.
I am 24 weeks pregnant with my first baby, and the pregnancy has been healthy so far.
I have a history of chronic high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol.
I have never had any surgeries or stays in the hospital.
I take prescription labetalol for my blood pressure and take daily prenatal vitamins.
I do not have any known allergies to medicines, latex, or foods.
I do not smoke, and I completely stopped drinking any alcohol once I became pregnant.
I work as an accountant and live in an apartment with my husband.
My mother has high blood pressure, but there are no other significant medical conditions in my family.
I thought maybe I picked up a tiny splinter or paper cut that got infected, and my pregnancy hormones caused it to blow up into this big blood blister.

I'm really worried this fast-growing red bump might be skin cancer, and I'm terrified that any numbing medicine or procedure could harm my baby. I'm hoping you can safely take this off or burn it away today using medicine that won't hurt my pregnancy so it stops bleeding all over my clothes and sheets.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 126/82 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 °C, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
An alert, well-nourished pregnant woman appearing comfortable, holding a dry gauze dressing over her right thumb.

A 1-cm pedunculated, bright red, friable vascular nodule on the volar pad of the right thumb with a collarette of scale and minor contact bleeding upon palpation; remainder of skin shows no dysplastic moles or similar lesions.
No palpable axillary or epitrochlear lymphadenopathy bilaterally.
Normal active and passive range of motion of the right thumb joints without joint effusion or deformity.
Radial pulses are 2+ bilaterally with prompt digital capillary refill under two seconds.
